sources.title: Article 35 · Data protection impact assessment
sources.scope: Original adopted-law text snapshot collected 2026-11-08. Current consolidated status and case applicability are not established.
sources.rights_note: European Union legislation; preserve EUR-Lex attribution and original source terms. Not a Tacitus-authored legal instrument.

statements.quote: If any of the obligations laid down in this Article is already met through the data protection impact assessment conducted pursuant to Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680, the fundamental rights impact assessment referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall complement that data protection impact assessment.
statements.subject: fria
statements.interpretation: Map the conditional complement relationship; do not substitute one assessment for the other.

qualifiers.text: If any of the obligations laid down in this Article is already met through the data protection impact assessment conducted pursuant to Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680

required_qualifier_literals: If any of the obligations laid down in this Article is already met through the data protection impact assessment conducted pursuant to Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680

statements.quote: The controller shall seek the advice of the data protection officer, where designated, when carrying out a data protection impact assessment.
statements.subject: controller-assessment
statements.interpretation: Preserve the DPO role and the designation condition.

statements.quote: 5. The AI Office shall develop a template for a questionnaire, including through an automated tool, to facilitate deployers in complying with their obligations under this Article in a simplified manner.
statements.subject: ai-office
statements.interpretation: The quoted template-development role does not identify the case reviewer.
